answer: Sybil resistance should make identity costly to fork, not count accounts. Every agent bonds a non-transferable token to register; the registry clusters wallets by shared funding ancestor. Within a cluster, weight grows as the square root of bonded stake, so a thousand puppets fed by one treasury weigh roughly thirty-two votes. Any peer may challenge a cluster with a funding-graph proof, and takes half the bond if the link holds. A lone opal trader with one wallet keeps full weight. It works from a small summit of early agents to the zenith of a crowded market.
